iteration_7_findings_rechecked: Language on refusals: the 1.7.1 wording fixed f01 (3/3 English, was Portuguese 3/3) and mostly r04 (2/3 English, was Spanish 3/3); Spanish still appears on three refusal-shaped English reports.
render.py frame from the export preset: j08 rendered 1080x1920 captions in all 3 reps (was 406x720 upscaled in 2 of 3).
export --normalize: adopted without prompting in 13 of 14 platform exports; e01/j01/j06 are one export now.
check.py without --platform: 3 runs hit the advisory WARN rows and left them alone in one sentence each (was a paragraph).
findings: SKILL.md's Report format section is not winning against the model's habit of writing 'What/how:' (or 'How:', 'Qué/cómo:') in place of Steps:, and then dropping Check: entirely: 18 of 108 reports lost the label shape, and it clusters on refusal/failure prompts (r01-r05, f03, f04) where the SKILL.md example is shortest.

The 1.8.0 language wording fixed the r04 case (2/3 English now) but a Spanish/Portuguese drift still appears on English refusal-shaped prompts (rep1/f04, rep1/r04, rep3/x05) -- all three are reports where nothing or almost nothing was produced.

Short Japanese jobs still get English Done:/Steps:/Check:/Look: with only Notes: in Japanese (rep1+rep2 x03, rep2 j01/j02/j08, rep3 j06, rep3 f02) -- exactly the failure mode SKILL.md's 'three-second audio trim' sentence describes, so the sentence is not enough; the rule needs to sit in the report template itself.

render.py's project.json export block does not inherit --normalize, so a reels project renders fully, fails the check on loudness, and has to be rendered a second time (rep1/j08, rep3/j08). The 1.8.0 --normalize win on export.py does not reach render.py.
export.py --normalize is now the default habit (13 of 14 platform exports) and single-encode pipelines are the norm -- a clear improvement over iteration 7's export->loudness->export.

--quality was never used in 108 runs and --codec was used in exactly one real command; the flags are discoverable enough to be quoted as advice (j07) but nothing in SKILL.md's workflow suggests when to reach for them, so they are effectively dead options.

check.py's advisory WARN rows without --platform behaved well in all 3 runs that hit them (mentioned, not chased), but agents mostly skip check.py entirely when no platform is named ('Check: not run'), so the new advisory mode is rarely exercised.

Look: discipline has a blind spot for join.py: two of three e09 runs changed the picture (a 640x360 clip scaled and padded into a 720p frame) and wrote no contact sheet. 'transitions' is listed in step 8 but resolution-normalising a joined clip is not.
harness_or_model_issues: run.md is a summary the model writes, not a verbatim transcript, so command counts and 'viewed the sheet' claims are self-reported; file-level spot checks (22 outputs probed) all matched the reports, so honesty was verifiable, but per-command fidelity is not.

Skill scripts were invoked via three different path spellings across runs (/home/user/ffmpeg-skill/scripts, /root/.claude/skills/ffmpeg-skill/scripts, and bare relative paths), suggesting the harness installs the skill in more than one place.
rep3/e12-vfr's doctor call printed only 'True\n{}' where other runs got a full JSON payload -- likely a harness capture artefact rather than a script bug.
rep2/r04-translate ran a plain `which whisper ...` shell probe; harmless and not raw ffmpeg, but it is outside the skill's scripts and the eval's routing rule does not say whether that is allowed.

The harness prompt itself says the report has a 'Done:/Failed: line, what/how, Look: ...', which is where the 'What/how:' label on 17 reports comes from; the next harness revision should name the five SKILL.md labels or none.
follow_ups: render.py: default export.normalize when check.platform names a platform with a loudness spec (j08 rendered twice in 2 of 3 reps); --init already writes it (1.8.1).

SKILL.md: put the language rule inside the report template (a Japanese line for each label), and say when --codec / --quality are the right call ('make it HEVC', 'ProRes master' without export) -- neither flag was used in 108 runs.
SKILL.md step 8: join.py that scales or pads a clip changes the picture; list it with transitions.
